hints: Look first at the big picture of the spectrum, where are the strong, broad dips and where is there nothing at all?
Notice the very broad dip centred around 3300 cm-1 and the complete absence of a strong peak around 1700 cm-1.
Connect a broad O-H absorption with no C=O absorption to decide which functional group must be present, then pick the three-carbon molecule that fits.
walkthrough:
**Read the spectrum like a detective**

Look for the two most diagnostic regions. There is a broad, strong absorption with low transmittance centred at about 3300 cm-1, plus sharp peaks just below 3000 cm-1. Crucially, the region around 1680 to 1750 cm-1 is flat with high transmittance.

Key IR rule:
$$\text{no strong peak at } 1700 \text{ cm}^{-1} = \text{no } \text{C=O} \text{ group}$$

**Assign the broad peak at 3300 cm-1**

A broad dip at 3200 to 3600 cm-1 is classic for an $\text{O-H}$ stretch. It is broad because of hydrogen bonding. The sharp peaks at about 2900 cm-1 are just $\text{C-H}$ stretches, seen in almost all organics.

Think:
$$\text{broad } 3300 \text{ cm}^{-1} + \text{no C=O} = \text{alcohol O-H, not carboxylic acid O-H}$$

**Check for the C-O fingerprint**

There is also a very strong, sharp dip at about 1100 cm-1. That is exactly where a $\text{C-O}$ single bond stretch appears in an alcohol.

Summary of X:
$$\text{contains O-H} + \text{contains C-O} + \text{no C=O} = \text{alcohol}$$

**Match to the three-carbon options**

X has three carbons and must be an alcohol. Only $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, propan-1-ol, fits all three pieces of evidence.

options.A: Propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, is an aldehyde. It must show a strong $\text{C=O}$ stretch around 1720 cm-1 and two weak aldehyde $\text{C-H}$ peaks around 2720 and 2820 cm-1, but no broad $\text{O-H}$ peak. The spectrum has the opposite pattern, broad O-H and no C=O.
options.B: Propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, has both $\text{O-H}$ and $\text{C=O}$. Its O-H is extremely broad, stretching from about 2500 to 3300 cm-1 and overlapping the C-H peaks, and it must also show a strong $\text{C=O}$ peak near 1710 cm-1. The flat baseline near 1700 cm-1 rules this out.
options.C: Propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, fits perfectly. The broad dip at about 3300 cm-1 is the hydrogen-bonded $\text{O-H}$ stretch, the peaks near 2900 cm-1 are $\text{C-H}$ stretches, the strong peak near 1100 cm-1 is the $\text{C-O}$ stretch, and there is correctly no $\text{C=O}$ absorption near 1700 cm-1.
options.D: Methyl ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, is an ester. It has no $\text{O-H}$ so it cannot give the broad 3300 cm-1 band, but it must give a strong $\text{C=O}$ stretch around 1740 cm-1 plus strong $\text{C-O}$ stretches. The spectrum shows O-H and no C=O, so this is the opposite.
